deep.reconstruction:
This page is not mathematics in progress. It is part of a letter from Ramanujan to Hardy, apparently written in 1917 while Hardy was preparing their joint paper 'Asymptotic formulae in combinatory analysis' (Proc. London Math. Soc. 1918). The earlier announcement of that work was the Comptes Rendus note of 1917. The previous and next pages hold unrelated Rogers–Ramanujan continued-fraction identities, so they are a different sheet of the same correspondence.

(A) Erratum request about (1.61).
- Ramanujan asks Hardy to add a footnote above result (1.61) of the partition paper.
- The footnote should say that the Comptes Rendus note misstated an error figure for p(61) = 1121505.
- He believes the CR note gave it as -44.641, while the correct value is -34.641.
- He adds that Hardy should first check whether the CR note gave the figures at all.
- My interpretation: the phrase 'p(61) over p(61)' most likely means the excess of a truncated asymptotic approximation p_1(61) (one or a few terms of the Hardy–Ramanujan series) over the true p(61). A difference of about 34.6 is the right size for the second-term correction at n = 61. I am not certain which truncation is meant.

(B) Correction to the previous day's letter.
- He had written fractions of the form π^2/(sin πα sin πβ), π^3/(sin πα sin πβ sin πγ), etc., but 'inverted them in haste'.
- So the fractions in that letter should be read upside down relative to what he first wrote.
- These are the leading coefficients of the singular parts of quantities like 1/((1-x^α)(1-x^β)...) or Γ(s)Γ(1-s)-type products, i.e. asymptotics for partitions into parts from restricted sets. The exact context cannot be recovered from this page.

(C) Proposed table.
- He suggests tabulating, for each s from 1 to 18, the maximum M_s and minimum m_s of |A_s(n)| over n.
- Here A_s(n) is the Hardy–Ramanujan exponential sum: A_q(n) = Σ_{h mod q, (h,q)=1} ω_{h,q} e^{-2πinh/q}, with ω_{h,q} = e^{πi s(h,q)} and s(h,q) the Dedekind sum.
- His entries: s=1: 1, 1. s=2: 1, 1. s=3: 2cos(π/18), 2sin(π/9). s=4: 2cos(π/8), 2sin(π/8).

Verification (my computation):
- A_1 = 1.
- A_2(n) = ±1.
- q=3: s(1,3) = 1/18 and s(2,3) = -1/18. Hence A_3(n) = 2cos(π/18 - 2πn/3). Its values for n ≡ 0, 1, 2 are 2cos(π/18) ≈ 1.9696, -2sin(π/9) ≈ -0.6840 and -2cos(5π/18) ≈ -1.2856. So max |A_3| = 2cos(π/18) and min = 2sin(π/9).
- q=4: s(1,4) = 1/8. Hence A_4(n) = 2cos(π/8 - πn/2), whose values are ±2cos(π/8) and ±2sin(π/8). So max = 2cos(π/8) and min = 2sin(π/8).
- All of Ramanujan's entries are correct.
- The published paper does contain a table of A_q(n) for q up to 18, so this suggestion appears to be the origin of that table.
errors: No mathematical errors in the table entries for s=1..4; they are correct.
The numerical claim (CR gave -44.641 instead of -34.641) cannot be checked from this page. Ramanujan himself is unsure whether the CR note gave the figure at all.
The ambiguous wording 'error of p(61) over p(61)' presumably means the excess of the truncated asymptotic formula over p(61); this is my interpretation.
He uses the letter s both as the table index and implicitly in the notation c_s(n)/A_s(n); this could be confused with Dedekind sums s(h,k), but it is only notation.

deep.surprise_reason: This is editorial correspondence with Hardy about the joint partition paper: an erratum, a correction of a slip, and a suggestion for a table that appeared in print. The A_q(n) values are correct but routine, and the Ramanujan–Hardy letters of 1917 are published and commented on (e.g. Berndt–Rankin).

checkable.asserts: A_3(n) takes the values 2cos(pi/18), -2sin(pi/9), -2cos(5pi/18); max |A_3| = 2cos(pi/18), min = 2sin(pi/9)
p(61) = 1121505, against which the error -34.641 of the truncated Hardy–Ramanujan approximation would be measured

transcription_corrections: The archival heading reads 'Add Ms a 94 17(11)' with folio '(104)'; this matches the transcription.
The quantity in the table is written '|c_s(n)|' (it looks like C with a subscript); it refers to the Hardy–Ramanujan sum A_s(n) of the partition paper.

The minimum entry for s=3 is '2 sin π/9' and the maximum is '2 cos π/18'. The s=4 entries are '2 cos π/8' and '2 sin π/8' (the π/8 in the sine is partly struck and overwritten). The '[?]' marks can be removed; the values are confirmed by computation.
The '&c' after the second fraction in the 'yesterday's letter' line is written in the margin and is legible.
